transcript: In this economics lecture, we discussed market equilibrium determined by the intersection of supply and demand curves. The law of demand establishes an inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded, holding all else equal. Conversely, the law of supply demonstrates that higher prices incentivize suppliers to produce more. When market forces operate freely without artificial price ceilings or price floors, price naturally adjusts to balance quantity supplied and demanded. Shifts in demand or supply occur through external factors such as consumer income, production costs, consumer preferences, and technological breakthroughs.
target_summary: Market equilibrium is established at the intersection of supply and demand curves, where price adjusts to clear the market. While price changes cause movements along the curve, external shocks—such as production input costs and consumer preferences—shift curves, creating new equilibrium pricing and quantities.
